chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from Salih ibn al-Sindi, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Hadda', from Abu Usama, from Abu Ubaydah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The mosque of Kufa is a garden from the gardens of Paradise; a thousand prophets and seventy prophets prayed in it. Its right side is mercy and its left side is cunning. In it is the staff of Moses (peace be upon him) and the tree of Qatyn, and the seal of Solomon (peace be upon him). From it is 'the oven gushed forth' and the ship sailed, and it is the pouch of Babylon, and the gathering place of the prophets (peace be upon them).

key_terms.رَوْضَةٌ مِنْ رِيَاضِ الْجَنَّةِ: A garden from the gardens of Paradise
key_terms.فَارَ التَّنُّورُ: The oven gushed forth (reference to Noah's flood)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual significance and historical contents of the Mosque of Kufa according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from the Tahdhib al-Ahkam, Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) elevates the status of the Mosque of Kufa by identifying it as a 'garden of Paradise' where 1,070 prophets offered prayer, linking it to key events in prophetic history. The narration highlights the presence of sacred relics such as the staff of Moses, the seal of Solomon, and the tree of Qatyn, while also connecting the site to the miraculous gushing of the oven and the sailing of Noah's Ark. This serves to establish Kufa not merely as a local center of worship, but as a cosmic hub of divine history and a gathering place for the prophets.
